outline: 1388 Mental Shortcuts for Adding and Subtracting Integers

examples.solution_text:
There are $5$ equal gaps from $0$ to $10$.
Each gap represents $10\div5=2$.

From $0$, count left: $-2,\ -4,\ -6,\ -8,\ -10,\ -12$.
$A$ is $6$ gaps left of $0$.
$B$ is $2$ gaps left of $0$.
From $0$, count right: $2,\ 4,\ 6$.
$C$ is $3$ gaps right of $0$.
$D$ is halfway between the ticks for $14$ and $16$, so it represents $15$.

$A=-12$.
$B=-4$.
$C=6$.
$D=15$.
Mark $-6$ at the third tick to the left of $0$.

[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}[x=0.3cm,y=0.6cm]
\draw[<->] (-21,0) -- (21,0);
\foreach \v in {-20,-18,...,20} {\draw (\v,0.13) -- (\v,-0.13);}
\foreach \v in {-20,-10,0,10,20} {\node[below] at (\v,-0.13) {$\v$};}
\fill (-6,0) circle (2pt);
\node[above] at (-6,0.2) {$-6$};
\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]

The labels $-6$ and $-7$ are one gap apart.
Each gap represents $1$.

Count upwards from $-6$: $-5,\ -4$.
Count downwards from $-8$: $-9$.
Count downwards from $-11$: $-12$.

The missing labels, from top to bottom, are $-4,\ -5,\ -9,\ -12$.

examples.derivation: Five equal gaps span 0 to 5, so each gap represents 1. A lies three gaps left of zero, giving -3; B lies four gaps right, giving 4. The question coordinates and solution annotations agree. Supported by the equal-interval teaching at lines 216–229 and source number-line exercises.

Four equal gaps span 0 to 20, so each gap represents 20÷4=5. A is three gaps left of zero, giving -15. Mia incorrectly treats each gap as 1. Both diagrams agree with this scale and position. This adapts Development Q14, lines 413–418 and image23.png, using different values.
